findings.issue:
The library compiles the draft 2019-09 keyword $recursiveRef under draft 2020-12 as a static reference, but the rule walk never sees it. Its target is not walked live, not counted, and not listed in w.targets or checkOrder, and the reference itself is never checked. Any walk-time bound or rule can therefore be bypassed by pointing a $recursiveRef at a subtree that nothing else references.

Probe files: <scratchpad>/r9/q/zz_r9g_test.go, zz_r9h_test.go and zz_r9i_test.go, plus overlay.json. Build: `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -c -o <scratchpad>/r9/q/probe.test -overlay <scratchpad>/r9/q/overlay.json ./internal/filter/validation/jsonschema/`. Run from the package directory: `<scratchpad>/r9/q/probe.test -test.run 'TestR9RecursiveRef' -test.v -test.count=1`. Machine load was 1.3 to 2.3.

(1) Panic. The 260-byte `{"$recursiveRef":"#/x","x":{"type":[1e9999999,2e9999999,...,21e9999999]}}` panics with a nil pointer dereference in CompileSchema, Check and Factory.Build (TestR9RecursiveRefCheck). The panic is in math/big.(*Rat).Num, reached from the library's duplicates/writeHash during the meta-schema check of /x. Nothing in hub recovers a PolicyCheck panic, so stage H crashes in every binary. This is the round-6 blocker shape, which the walk now refuses under $ref.

(2) Number bounds. An allOf of 300 `{"minimum":1e99999N}` under /x (6,339 bytes) compiles without RZ-CFG-005 in 10.1 s; 256 KiB would take minutes. The same control under $ref is refused in 0.2 ms at /x/allOf/0/minimum.

(3) Pattern bounds. Seven patterns of 400×[a-z]{1000} under /x (30,951 bytes) compile in 1.9 s, allocate 1,279 MB and keep 118 MB. One pattern of 30×[a-z]{1000} is refused under $ref but accepted under $recursiveRef.

(4) MaxSubschemas. `{"$recursiveRef":"#/x","x":{"allOf":[40,000 × {}]}}` (120 KB) takes 17.2 s before it is refused, and then only by fan-out. The same document with $ref is refused in 32 ms.

(5) Loader. `{"$recursiveRef":"https://example.com/x"}` and `{"$recursiveRef":"file:///etc/passwd"}` reach the loader: spyLoader records the URL, which violates FuzzCompileSchema's property and T15. The finding is then reported at the document root instead of at /$recursiveRef. The refusing loader still blocks any actual file or network access.

(6) Round-8 fix bypass. `{"$recursiveRef":"#/additionalItems","additionalItems":{"multipleOf":0}}` compiles, and Factory.Build succeeds. Schema.Validate(5) and Filter.Handle(onRequestBody, application/json, `5`) then panic with 'division by zero'. The executor turns this into 503 RZ-RT-011 under closed, or skips validation under open.

This is not a regression; no run record mentions $recursiveRef.

findings.issue:
Long member names in a schema's keyword maps make the library's quadratic queue search compare long location prefixes, so a small schema can stall stage H and the Node for tens of seconds. When the library enqueues a subschema, it compares that subschema's location with every queued schema's location. Sibling locations of equal length share the parent's whole location prefix, so each comparison scans the full prefix: a single property name of N bytes above K sibling positions costs about K²/2 × N bytes of memequal. The compiled Schema also keeps every position's location string, prefix included. No rule bounds the bytes of a name or a location: MaxSchemaBytes bounds the document and MaxSubschemas only the count of positions. Non-ASCII names grow about 3 times once the library percent-encodes them in its locations.

Probe: <scratchpad>/r9/p/zz_r9_test.go (TestR9Deep, TestR9DeepKept), overlaid. findings.issue:
The work model charges each step of the dynamic-scope walk at 4 units whatever the length of the $dynamicAnchor name. At every $dynamicRef evaluation, resolveDynamicAnchor walks the whole scope chain and runs `scp.sch.resource.dynamicAnchors[name]` at each step; that lookup compares or hashes the full anchor name, so each step costs time proportional to the name's length. The walker does not bound anchor names, and a name of about 120 KB fits within MaxSchemaBytes. The real cost is then more than 100 times the charge.

Probe: <scratchpad>/r9/zz_r9_test.go (TestR9DynamicAnchor, TestR9DynamicAnchorBig), overlaid with -overlay and built with -o into the scratchpad. Each case goes through Factory.Build and Handle(onRequestBody, application/json) at the 10 MiB default; load 0.2 to 0.9. Schema: {"$dynamicAnchor":"<A>","items":{"$dynamicRef":"#<A>"}}. Body: an array of n arrays, each nested 58 deep around the number 1 (valid; passes every check).
- n=50 (5,901 B), A of 1 byte: 5.3 ms for 5,758,792 units charged (0.92 ns/unit).
- Same body, A of 1,000 bytes: 16.7 ms (2.9 ns/unit).
- Same body, A of 100,000 bytes: 650 ms (112.8 ns/unit).
- n=2000 (236,001 B, 2.25% of the limit), A of 120,000 bytes (schema 240,049 B, built in 8 ms): Handle returns Continue after 33.1 s of uncancellable CPU in the decision pass alone, charged 230,336,392 units, 8.6% of the 2,684,354,560-unit work limit. At 143.8 ns/unit, a body at the work limit (about 2.7 MB) would hold a core for about 386 s.

CPU profile (n=300): memeqbody 97.7%, via internal/runtime/maps.(*Map).getWithoutKeySmallFastStr, called from validator.resolveDynamicAnchor and validateRefs. With nine or more anchors in a resource the lookup hashes the name instead, at the same per-byte cost.
findings.fix:
- Charge the anchor name's bytes at every scope step: record in workFlags the longest $dynamicAnchor/$dynamicRef anchor name (or each state's), then in enter add `mulCap(evals, mulCap(frames, scopeUnits + longestAnchor/nameHashBytes))`. Also charge once per $dynamicRef evaluation for its own `sch.DynamicAnchor == dref.Anchor` comparison.
- Alternatively, bound anchor name length with a new RZ-CFG-005 rule; that needs a contract request against 07 req 75 and R-77.
- Add a long-anchor case to workCases so BenchmarkWorkModel reports it.
- Add a TestWorkCharges row that pins the per-byte term.
- Cite R-77 and 07 section 9 item 21.

- Use an x-probe keyword at the deepest link of each branch that runs runtime.GC and records HeapAlloc, as decisionTree does (and as the round-8 reviewer's probe did); assert the live heap stays flat across branches and within the chain's charge.

minors.issue:
[lenses: integration, code] Regression introduced this round in an edge case: an unreferenced additionalItems subschema is now refused when it holds an identifier and its content breaks the 2020-12 meta-schema, even though nothing compiles or applies it. identifies() marks the subtree live, compileWalked compiles it, and the new checkApart meta-checks it. contractRequests: Architecture R-77, 07 reqs 80 and 82 (major 3 fix, proposed): the working-set, reservation and work limits scale from max(limits.maxRequestBodyBytes, MinScaledLimit = 128 KiB), so below 128 KiB they are 1 MiB, 1.5 MiB and 2^25 work units, and 'at most 8 (12) times the limit' holds from 128 KiB up. The decoded limit still scales from the raw limit (R-63). Reason: the parts that do not grow with the body (the decision wrapper's 24 KiB, an 8 KiB stack frame per evaluation of each chain on the path, a 32 KiB+ matcher, the evaluations at the root) exceeded 8x the limit below about 32 KiB, so {} got 413 at 1 and 2 KiB and a 616-byte composed order at 16 KiB. Every maxRequestBodyBytes now works for small bodies; record that no smallest workable limit exists beyond the decoded limit.

Architecture R-77 and 07 reqs 80 to 82 (major 3, replacing fix6's job-stack request): record the backtracker job-stack window as an accepted consequence. With the floor, up to 128 KiB a string of about 20,400 to 37,400 bytes under ^[^<>]*$ (7 instructions, 1 job per position) and of about 5,100 to 20,100 bytes under ^(?:[a-z]+|[0-9]+|\s)*$ (13 instructions, 4 jobs per position) is 413. At 256 KiB the first never binds and the second binds from about 10,600 bytes (4% of the limit). From 512 KiB neither binds, and from about 1.6 MiB no pattern does. Matching with the NFA simulation only (regexp MatchReader) would remove the window, but was measured at 2 to 12 times the backtracker's time on common patterns.

07 reqs 75 and 76, architecture R-77 (major 2 fix, replacing r7 minor 1's request text): every schema position the library compiles but no meta-schema check of the library covers (below additionalItems, compiled through a JSON Pointer reference, an anchor or an $id) is checked against the draft 2020-12 meta-schema by the compile, before the library compiles it. Each finding is RZ-CFG-005 with the meta-schema's own message, as the same subschema gets under $defs. Below an additionalItems the library never compiles, nothing is checked. $schema is checked everywhere and references only where the library compiles them. Identifiers count only as strings of schema positions.

Architecture R-77 and 07 reqs 80 to 82 (major 4 fix): the unevaluated-tracking maps are charged per evaluation of the longest in-place chain at a value (min of the evaluations that may copy and the chain), as the stack is, not per evaluation, because the library drops a branch's copy when it merges it. The work terms keep counting every evaluation.

Architecture R-77, 07 req 90 and F6 (blocker fix): add to the compile figures that states of 500 members, each applying a thousand patterns or a thousand kinds of length, compile in 0.14 to 0.17 s (before: 2.9 s / 2.4 GB and 1.05 s). stateBudget now also charges the programs of each schema's pattern reach. The combined worst cases (0.95 to 1.2 s) remain as already requested.

filter.Factory contract (WP-01) and WP-70 (minor 3, repeated): record that Build returns ctx.Err() and non-finding filter.Shared failures without an RZ code, as an operational failure of the snapshot compile, not a rejection of the Revision. Build's doc comment now cites this request.
